_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 6 Sounds Near and Far. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. The five chapters follow LESSON["lecture"] in content/lesson-6.py, part for part, in its own words and examples: the drum, bell, bird and rain; the elastic band and the hum; the bell and the child who walks six steps away (the lesson's soundFar drawing); the loud, medium, quiet table; the sound makers used safely. The film is silent apart from the voice, so every sound is SHOWN as rings spreading from its source.
title: Sounds Near and Far
subtitle: Grade 1 Science
objectives: Explore that as sound travels from a source it becomes quieter.
Identify the senses (limited to sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch) and what they detect, linking each to the correct body part.
Collect and record observations and/or measurements by annotating images and completing simple tables.
Follow instructions safely when doing practical work.

beats.say: A bell rings. Right next to it, the sound is loud. Far away, it is quiet.
Where do sounds come from? What makes them? And why do they get quieter?
Tap a drum. Ring a bell. A bird sings. Rain falls.
Every sound comes from somewhere. The thing that makes it is called the source.
Boom. The drum is the source of that sound. Tweet. The bird is the source.
You hear with your ears. That is your sense of hearing.
Ears hear the sound. They do not make it. The drum makes it.
Pluck an elastic band. It shakes so fast it looks blurry.
And you hear a twang. A sound is made when something shakes very fast.
Scientists have a word for fast shaking. They call it vibrating.
Hum, and put your hand on your throat. You can feel it shaking.
Touch the band to stop it shaking. No shaking, no sound.
Stand right next to the bell and ring it. It is loud.
Take a step back and ring it again. It is quieter.
Keep going, all six steps. Every step, the sound gets quieter.
The bell is rung the same every time. It does not make a quieter sound.
The sound gets quieter on its way to you. It spreads out as it travels.
The further a sound travels, the quieter it gets.
Sounds can be loud, medium or quiet. A drum next to you is loud.
A whisper is quiet. You have to stand close to hear it.
You can write it down in a table, like a scientist.
One step from the bell, it was loud. Three steps, medium.
Six steps, quiet. The further away, the quieter it gets.
Your ears hear sounds. Very loud sounds can hurt them.
Never shout into someone's ear. Never bang a drum next to your head.
Use sound makers carefully. Hit a drum gently, with the stick.
If a sound hurts, cover your ears and move away.
Every sound has a source. A sound is made when something shakes.
The further a sound travels from its source, the quieter it gets.
You can write loud, medium and quiet in a table.
And your ears hear it all, so look after them.
